questions.question: On the basis of status of development, how are resources classified?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Potential, developed stock, and reserves.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Resources are classified on the basis of their status of development which includes potential, developed stock, and reserves.**
 
• Potential resources are those that are **not yet developed but are believed to exist in a particular area.** For example, minerals in a particular region that are yet to be explored.
 
• Developed stock resources are those that are currently being used and are available in the environment. For example, forests, fisheries, and wildlife.
 
• Reserves are the resources that have been identified and are available for use in the future. For example, fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas.
 
• Biotic resources are living resources such as forests, fisheries, and wildlife, while abiotic resources are non-living resources such as minerals, rocks, and water.
 
• Renewable resources are those that can be replenished naturally over time, such as solar, wind, and hydro energy. Non-renewable resources are those that cannot be replenished naturally, such as fossil fuels.

questions.question: The 101st constitution amendment act of the Indian Constitution introduced the system of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Introduced GST (Goods and Services Tax).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 101st Amendment Act, 2016 Introduced GST (Goods and Services Tax).
 
• The 101 Constitutional Amendment Act was instrumental in conducting in India's Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• The Goods and Services Tax replaced all the erstwhile indirect taxes that were levied on the manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services across the country.
 
• The fundamental objective of GST was to build a common market with a constant tax rate in India.
 
• The goods and services tax eradicates the initial taxes for the same transaction as input tax credits.
 
• It seeks to increase revenue as it brings more taxpayers by growing the tax base.

questions.question: Sunanda Nair completed her PhD from University of Mumbai for her thesis in "Intrinsic Lyrical Feminism" in which dance form?

questions.question: Who was appointed as the chairperson of Law Commission of India in November 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Justice Rituraj Awasthi__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India (GoI) appointed a Chairperson and Members of the 22nd Law Commission of India, which was notified on 24th February 2020.
 
• Justice Rituraj Awasthi, retired Chief Justice of Karnataka High Court is appointed as the chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission of India, and 4 others are appointed as members.
 
• The commission would have a tenure of 3 years with effect from the date of publication of the order of the Constitution in the Official Gazette.
 
• The 22nd law Commission was vacant since the retirement of former Supreme Court Judge Justice BS Chauhan in 2018.
 
• The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory body, under the Union Ministry of Law & Justice that was first constituted in 1955, by a notification of the GoI, for a definite term to carry out research in the field of law.
 
• Full-time members of the commission are Justice Ravi R. Tripathi and S. Siva Kumar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ Law Commission of India

 
• Law Commission of India is an executive body established by an order of the Government of India.
 
• The Commission's function is to research and advise the Government of India on legal reform, and is composed of legal experts, and headed by a retired judge.
 
• The commission is established for a fixed tenure and works as an advisory body to the Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the Joint Session of the Parliament of India?

options.text: So far, Joint sittings of the two Houses have taken place on three occasions.
The President can summon both the Houses to meet for the Joint Session.
The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) presides over a Joint Session.
Joint session is held to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses of the Parliament.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) presides over a Joint Session.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• In the absence of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker presides over it with regard to a joint sitting of the Parliament.
 
• It was the first time he addressed the newly elected 17th Loksabha.
 
• Article 108:__ 
 __
 
• Article 108 of the Indian Constitution of India provides for Joint sitting of both Houses. 
 
• The joint sitting of the Parliament is called by the President. 
 
• It is presided over by the Speaker__ or, in their absence, by the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha or in their absence, the Deputy-Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• __The Chairperson doesn't preside over the joint session at any means/cost__.
 
 
 
• In India, if an ordinary bill has been rejected by any house of the parliament and if more than six months have elapsed.
 
• The President may summon a joint session for purpose of passing the bill.
 
• The bill is passed by a simple majority of a joint sitting.
 
• 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] __Additional Information__

__
 
• All executive power is vested in the President of India.
 
• The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister aids and advises the President who exercises his powers in accordance with such advice.
 
• Constitutional Provision:__
 __
 
• Article 87 of the constitution provides two instances when the President specially addresses both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The President of India addresses both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
 
• Sabha at the beginning of the first session after each general election when the reconstituted lower house meets for the first time.
 
• The President also addresses both the houses at the beginning of the first session of each year.
 
 
 
• The President’s speech essentially highlights the government’s policy priorities and plans for the upcoming year.
 
• The address provides a broad framework of the government’s agenda and direction.
 
• Quorum:__
 __
 
• The quorum to constitute a joint sitting shall be one-tenth of the total number of members of the Houses.
 
 
 
• Procedure:__
 __
 
• The procedures of joint sessions are subject to modifications and variations as the Speaker may consider necessary or appropriate.
 
 
 
• Time of sitting:__
 __
 
• The duration and adjournment of the joint sitting shall be determined by the Speaker.
 
 
 
• Summons to members:__
 __
 
• The Secretary-General shall issue summons to each member specifying the time and place for a joint sitting.
 
 
 
• Apart from this, the joint sitting of both the houses is also held to resolve the deadlock over the passing of key legislation.
 
• Not all bills can be referred to a joint sitting of Parliament.
 
• There are two exceptions:__
 
 
• Money bill under Article 110.
 
• Constitution amendment bill under Article 368.

questions.question: As of November 2022, who is the President of Nationalist Congress Party, a political party in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sharad Pawar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Sharad Pawar is a veteran politician and a former Chief Minister of Maharashtra.
 
• He is one of the founders of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), which was formed in 1999 after he split from the Indian National Congress.
 
• The symbol is situated on a tri-colored Indian flag.
 
• The election symbol of NCP is an analog alarm clock.
 
• The clock is drawn in blue and has two legs and an alarm button.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), is a national political party in India.
 
• The NCP has described itself as a “millennial party with a modern and progressive orientation” with an ideology of “holistic democracy,” “Gandhian secularism,” and “federalism-based national unity.”
 
• It has called for a “democratic secular society wedded to equality and social justice.”
 
• The NCP was formally established in June 1999 in New Delhi by three former members of the Indian National Congress (Congress Party)—Sharad Pawar, Purno Sangma, and Tariq Anwar—after they had been expelled from that party for demanding that only a person born in India should be allowed to become the country’s president, vice president, or prime minister.
 
• The issue arose after Sonia Gandhi, the Italian-born widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, became leader of the Congress Party and thus ordinarily would become the candidate for prime minister if the party were to gain a parliamentary majority and form a government.
 
• Pawar was elected president of the NCP, and Sangma and Anwar became its general secretaries.
 
• None of the NCP’s election manifestos, however, has highlighted the foreigner issue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Supriya Sule, who is the daughter of Sharad Pawar, is a prominent leader of the NCP and a member of parliament from Baramati, Maharashtra. She is also the party's Deputy Leader in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Nawab Malik is another senior leader of the NCP and a member of the Maharashtra Legislative Council. He has held various positions in the party, including spokesperson and general secretary.
 
• Eknath Shinde is a leader of the Shiv Sena, which is a political party in Maharashtra and a former ally of the NCP. He is currently the Minister for Urban Development in the Maharashtra government.

questions.question: Export of manufactured goods ______ trade and commerce.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**expands.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **"expands," is the correct answer because exporting manufactured goods can lead to increased trade and commerce. **

 
 
• **By exporting goods, a company can expand its customer base beyond its domestic market, leading to increased sales and revenue.**
 
 
 
• "reduces," is incorrect because exporting goods typically leads to increased trade and commerce, not a reduction.
 
• "contracts," is also incorrect for the same reason as option 1.
 
• "weakens," is not a direct result of exporting manufactured goods and is therefore incorrect.
 
• The keyword "manufactured goods" refers to products that have been processed or transformed from raw materials into finished products. This can include anything from electronics to clothing to furniture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Trade balance:

 
• The balance of trade (BOT) is the difference between a country's imports and exports for a given period and is the most important component of a country's balance of payments (BOP).
 
• A trade deficit occurs when a country buys more goods and services than it exports in terms of value, whereas a trade surplus occurs when a country exports more goods and services than it imports.
 
• The phrase "trade" relates to the purchase and sale of things. When it is done on a global basis, however, it is referred to as imports and exports.

questions.question: The chemical formula of washing soda is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na2CO3. 10H2O.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Washing soda is a white crystalline powder that is used in laundry detergents and as a water softener.**

 
 
• The chemical formula of washing soda is Na₂CO₃.10H₂O, which means it contains two sodium atoms, one carbon atom, three oxygen atoms, and ten water molecules.
 
 
 
• Ca(OH)₂ is calcium hydroxide, which is used in construction, as a flocculant in wastewater treatment, and as a food additive.
 
• Na₂SO₄ is sodium sulfate, which is used in the manufacture of detergents, glass, and paper, as well as in the textile and leather industries.
 
• NaHCO₃ is sodium bicarbonate, which is used as a leavening agent in baking and as an antacid to treat heartburn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sodium Carbonate is the chemical name for ‘washing soda’ (**Na2CO3.10H2O**.).
 
• It is the water-soluble sodium salt of carbonic acid.
 
• It is well known domestically for its everyday use as a water softener.
 
• Washing soda is produced using Solvay's process.
 
• The process includes the reaction of Sodium Chloride with ammonia, and carbon dioxide, in water.
 
• Carbon Dioxide is produced through calcium carbonate from which calcium oxide that gets left is used in ammonia recovery from ammonium chloride.
 
 
• **NaHCO3** is **Sodium Bicarbonate**.**​**

questions.question: Currency notes and coins are called fiat money. They are also called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Legal tender.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Fiat money is a type of currency that has no intrinsic value and is not backed by a physical commodity like gold or silver.
 
• Legal tender refers to the currency that is recognized by law as a valid means of payment for debts and taxes.
 
• Currency notes and coins are examples of fiat money because their value is determined by government decree, rather than any underlying value.
 
• Currency notes and coins are called fiat money. 
 
• They do not have intrinsic value like that of gold or silver coins. 
 
• Unlike commodity money, fiat money is not backed by any physical commodity instead it is backed by the order or authority of the government.
 
• They are also called legal tenders as they cannot be refused by any citizen of the country for settlement of any kind of transaction.
 
• The value of the currency notes and coins is derived from the guarantee provided by the issuing authority of these items. Every currency note bears on its face a promise from the Governor of RBI that if someone produces the note to RBI or any other commercial bank, RBI will be responsible for giving the person purchasing power equal to the value printed on the note.
 
• Fiat money gives central banks control over the economy because they decide how much currency has to be printed and in case if it prints too much, that can result in hyperinflation.
 
• Supply and demand relations in the market derive the value of Fiat Money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Legal tender laws vary by country but generally require individuals and businesses to accept the designated currency as payment for debts and taxes.
 
• Fiat money is the most common form of currency used today and is used by virtually every country in the world.
 
• Legal contracts, lease deeds, and loan deeds are all important legal documents used in various transactions, but they are not related to fiat money.

questions.question: The cytoplasm has ______ such as ribosomes, mitochondria, and Golgi bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** organelles.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Organelles are specialized structures within a cell that perform specific functions.** Ribosomes are responsible for protein** synthesis,** mitochondria produce energy for the cell,** and **Golgi bodies are involved in processing and packaging proteins.**
 
• The term "cytoplasm" refers to the **gel-like substance that fills a cell and surrounds the nucleus.** It contains various organelles and provides a medium for cellular processes to occur.
 
• "cells", is incorrect as the cytoplasm itself is a part of the cell and contains organelles.
 
• "organs", and option 4, "tissues", are incorrect as they refer to structures found in multicellular organisms, whereas the cytoplasm and its organelles are found within individual cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Cytoplasm:

 
• It is the jelly-like substance present between the cell membrane and the nucleus.
 
• Various other components, or organelles, of cells are present in the cytoplasm.
 
• These are mitochondria, Golgi bodies, ribosomes, etc.
 
• It facilitates material exchange and storage among cell organelles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05f249617f1db06e721d2dcdbef8a5abd7d4457422e911fe074d3ce913ad5319.png]

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Vakataka Dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vindhyashakti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Vindhyashakti was the founder of the Vakataka Dynasty, which ruled in central India from the 3rd to the 5th century CE.**
 
• ** He was succeeded by his son Pravarasena I, who expanded the dynasty's territory and established its capital at Vatsagulma (modern-day Washim in Maharashtra).**
 
• The Vakataka Empire was a dynasty of the Indian subcontinent, starting in the mid-3rd century CE from the Deccan.
 
• It was a Brahmin dynasty.
 
• It is noted that the Vakatakas were patrons of the arts, architecture, and literature.
 
• Under the patronage of emperor Vakataka, Harishena, the rock-cut Buddhist viharas and chaityas of Ajanta Caves (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) were built.
 
• Nagabhata I was an Indian king who founded the Pratihara dynasty of imperial Gurjara.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Pravarasena II,** another son of Vindhyashakti, was also a prominent ruler of the Vakataka Dynasty who is known for his patronage of the arts and literature.
 
• **Prabhavatigupta,** on the other hand, was not a founder of the Vakataka Dynasty but rather a queen who ruled over it during its later period. She was the daughter of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II and is known for her contributions to the arts and religion.
 
• It is important to note that the Vakataka Dynasty was contemporary with other prominent Indian dynasties such as the Guptas, the Pallavas, and the Chalukyas, and played a significant role in shaping the political and cultural landscape of ancient India.

questions.question: In 1928, the ______ was founded at a meeting in Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi. Amongst its leaders were Bhagat Singh, Jatin Das, and Ajoy Ghosh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• HSRA was founded by Ram Prasad Bismil and other important figures associated with HSRA are Chandrasekhar Azad, Ashfaqulla Khan, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Jatin das, Ajay Ghosh.
 
• The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was established in 1928.
 
• Revolutionaries like Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were present at the meeting, held at the Feroz Shah Kotla ground in Delhi, during the establishment of the organization.
 
• Bhagat Singh was involved in two high-profile plots against British authorities in India that helped galvanize the Indian independence movement. In 1928 he took part in a plot to kill the police chief responsible for the death of influential Indian writer and politician Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was an Indian nationalist whose defiance of British authority in India made him a hero among Indians, but his **wartime alliances with Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan left a legacy vexed by authoritarianism,** anti-Semitism, and military failure.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore, the Nobel laureate gave the title of 'Desh Nayak' to Subhash Chandra Bose in recognition of his service to the nation and its people.
 
• **Jatin Das **was an Indian independence activist and revolutionary who worked to make India independent from the British Raj and was a member of the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. He died in the Lahore Central Jail after a 63-day hunger strike.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• All India Depressed Classes Association was founded by B.R. Ambedkar in 1930 and aimed to uplift the socially and economically backward classes in India.
 
• Madras Presidency Association was founded in 1884 by C. Sankaran Nair and aimed to promote education and political rights for the people of Madras Presidency.
 
• Kabui Naga Association was founded in 1946 and aimed to promote the welfare of the Kabui Naga tribe in Manipur.

questions.question: West Bengal shares its longest border with which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **West Bengal is a state located in the eastern part of India and shares its borders with three countries, namely, Nepal, Bhutan, and Bangladesh.**
 
• Bangladesh is the country that shares the longest border with West Bengal, which is** approximately 2,217 km long.**
 
• The border between West Bengal and Bangladesh is a porous one, with many illegal crossings and smuggling activities taking place.
 
• The Indo-Bangladesh border is also known as the International Border (IB) and is guarded by the Border Security Force (BSF) on the Indian side and the Border Guards Bangladesh (BGB) on the Bangladeshi side.
 
• West Bengal has 3 international boundaries.
 
• West Bengal has international boundaries with Bangladesh in the east, Bhutan in the North, and Nepal in the northwest.
 
• West Bengal with 2,217 km (**1377.58** miles) shares the longest border with Bangladesh.
 
 
• It is the fifth-longest land border in the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhutan shares a 183 km long border** with West Bengal, which is mostly mountainous and forested.
 
• **Nepal shares a 1,751 km** long border with India, of which 97 km is shared with West Bengal. This border is also mostly mountainous and forested.
 
• **Myanmar shares a 1,643 km** long border with India, of which 262 km is shared with West Bengal. This border is also known as the Indo-Myanmar border and is guarded by the Assam Rifles on the Indian side.
 
• **China shares a 3,488 km** long border with India, of which 1,597 km is shared with the state of Arunachal Pradesh. West Bengal does not share a border with China.

questions.question: Three of the following four are auxiliaries to trade and therefore form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Warehousing is an important auxiliary to trade as it helps in storing goods and maintaining their quality until they reach the market.**
 
• Transportation is also crucial for trade as it enables the movement of goods from one place to another, facilitating trade between regions and countries.
 
• Insurance is another important auxiliary to trade as it helps mitigate the risks associated with trade by providing financial protection against losses due to unforeseen events.
 
• **Agriculture, on the other hand, is the primary sector of the economy that involves the cultivation of crops and the raising of livestock, which are then processed and sold in the market. While it is a crucial sector for the overall economic development of a country, it is not directly related to trade as an auxiliary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Insurance is a means of protection from financial loss in which, in exchange for a fee, a party agrees to compensate another party in the event of a certain loss, damage, or injury. It is a form of risk management, primarily used to hedge against the risk of a contingent or uncertain loss.
 
• Warehousing is when you purchase goods from a manufacturer and store them before they are shipped to another location for fulfillment. You may store these goods in a warehouse, spare room, or other facilities. This all depends on how much stock you have, and how big your business is
 
• Transportation is the movement of goods and persons from place to place and the various means by which such movement is accomplished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d55b2a06c4566ae1b1ed0acea1e72a61f10e2cc4c1491fd914968c7fe6e5140.png]
